landmarks.name: Fort Zeelandia
landmarks.writeup: A historic fortress in Paramaribo, originally built by the British and later expanded by the Dutch, symbolizing colonial history.

wiki.extract: Fort Zeelandia is a fortress in Paramaribo, Suriname. In 1640 the French built a wooden fort on the spot which, during British colonial period, was reinforced and became Fort Willoughby. It was taken by the Dutch in 1667 and renamed Fort Zeelandia.

landmarks.name: Central Suriname Nature Reserve
landmarks.writeup: A UNESCO World Heritage site known for its pristine tropical rainforest and biodiversity.

wiki.extract:
The Central Suriname Nature Reserve is a conservation unit in Suriname.
It preserves an area of tropical rainforest. The reserve is in pristine condition.

landmarks.name: Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral
landmarks.writeup: One of the tallest wooden structures in the Western Hemisphere, located in Paramaribo.

wiki.extract: The Cathedral-Basilica of Saint Peter and Paul, also called Saint Peter and Paul Cathedral, is a wooden Roman Catholic cathedral located in the centre of the capital city of Paramaribo, Suriname.

cultural_events.name: Maroon Festival
cultural_events.writeup: Celebrates the culture and history of the Maroon communities with music, dance, and traditional rituals.

wiki.extract: Maroon 5 is an American pop rock band formed in Los Angeles, California. It consists of lead vocalist and guitarist Adam Levine, rhythm guitarist and keyboardist Jesse Carmichael, lead guitarist James Valentine, drummer Matt Flynn, keyboardist PJ Morton, and bassist and keyboardist Sam Farrar. Original members Levine, Carmichael, bassist Mickey Madden, and drummer Ryan Dusick first came together as Kara's Flowers in February 1994, while they were in high school.

cultural_events.name: Keti Koti
cultural_events.writeup: Commemorates the abolition of slavery in Suriname with festivities and remembrance events.

wiki.extract: Ketikoti, sometimes spelled as Keti Koti, or officially Dag der Vrijheden, is an annual celebration on 1 July that marks Emancipation Day in Suriname. The day is also known as Manspasi Dei or Prisiri Manspasi, meaning "Emancipation" or "Emancipation Festival", or Kettingsnijden.

food_writeup: Surinamese cuisine is a diverse blend of Indian, African, Indonesian, Chinese, and Dutch influences, featuring dishes like roti, pom, and peanut soup.
brief_history: Suriname was originally inhabited by indigenous peoples before becoming a Dutch colony in the 17th century. It gained independence in 1975 and has a multicultural society shaped by African, Asian, and European influences.

important_people.name: Johan Adolf Pengel
important_people.description: influential politician and former Prime Minister

current_conflicts: Suriname is generally peaceful with no significant internal or external conflicts reported as of 2024.

commentary.inflation_management: Suriname's inflation is a story of exchange-rate regimes breaking. Under the pegged SRD, inflation ran 6.4-17.7% through 2006-2011 (17.7% in 2011 after a devaluation), then calmed to 1.9-6.9% in 2012-2015. When gold and oil prices collapsed in 2015-16, the peg gave way: inflation hit 55.5% in 2016 and 22% in 2017. A brief calm (4.4-6.9% in 2018-2019) ended with the 2020 crisis and the move to a floating/unified exchange rate: 34.9% in 2020, 59.1% in 2021, 52.4% in 2022, and 51.6% in 2023. Under the IMF program's reserve-money targeting, disinflation finally took hold: 16.2% in 2024 and a projected 9.2% in 2025 - still high, but the first single-digit reading in a decade. The central bank's credibility is being rebuilt from near zero.
commentary.debt_management: Suriname's debt record is one of the region's worst boom-bust cycles. The ratio was a modest 22.5% of GDP in 2006 and 14.6% in 2009, then climbed as gold and oil revenues collapsed: 25.2% in 2014, 41.2% in 2015, 75.4% in 2016, and 84% in 2019, before the 2020 default and COVID devaluation detonated it to 146.4% - the series high. Under the 2021 IMF Extended Fund Facility ($688m, 36 months) and the November 2023 bondholder restructuring (the $550m 2026 Eurobond and other bonds exchanged for a new 2033 bond at a ~29% haircut, plus an oil-linked value recovery instrument tied to Block 58), it fell to 115.8% in 2021, 97.7% in 2023, and 88% in 2024 - then rose again to a projected 105.8% in 2025 on currency effects. Paris Club and bilateral (China, India) restructurings accompanied the program. Sustainability now depends on the GranMorgu oil project (FID late 2024, first oil expected ~2028) actually delivering the revenues the VRI promises.

key_events.event: Desi Bouterse elected; gold and oil revenues funded an unsustainable spending boom.

$478m IMF program went off track and was cancelled in 2017; government issued a $550m 9.25% Eurobond.

commentary.outlook_next_decade: Suriname's outlook is binary and oil-linked. If GranMorgu delivers first oil around 2028 as planned, royalties transform the fiscal picture, the VRI pays bondholders, and debt falls fast - the IMF program has already done the hard institutional work. If oil disappoints or is delayed, the 2025 uptick in debt (105.8%) is a warning that the old dynamics - weak revenues, currency pressure - reassert themselves. The base case is cautiously positive given FID and the new government's reform mandate, but this is the highest-uncertainty outlook in the region: one project, one commodity, and a political system that has defaulted before. Honest assessment: the next five years are a coin flip with good odds.
commentary.caveat: Outlook is an analytical assessment as of October 2026, not a forecast. 2025 figures are IMF estimates/projections.
